title: German Registry for Children and Adolescents with Alpha‑1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD).
summary:
Background
Alpha‑1‑antitrypsin deficiency is a rare hereditary shortage of an important protein in the body. It can already cause severe liver problems in childhood and adolescence. Many details, however, remain unknown. How often this deficiency occurs in Germany, for example, and which signs indicate a severe course in childhood and adolescence have not been well studied so far. Therefore a nationwide patient registry is to be established that records affected children and adolescents and improves their care. Participation in the registry is carried out by the families themselves.  

Research question
The study aims, among other things, to determine how common alpha‑1‑antitrypsin deficiency is among children and adolescents in Germany, which characteristics (e.g., clinical findings, laboratory values) signal that the disease will take a particularly severe course in childhood, and what measures are needed to improve support for the families.  

Methodology
All children and adolescents diagnosed with the deficiency can be entered into the registry by their parents or legal guardians. Families receive a simple way to participate via a free smartphone app (“Alpha 1 KIDS”) or via the Internet. After registration, the registry collects, for example, basic information on health status, laboratory results, and clinical course.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Homozygous alpha‑1 antitrypsin deficiency.
Exclusion criteria:
Absent of consent
